title: Token by Token — an introduction to the lab and its methodology

claims.text: Token by Token is an open inference lab.

source.excerpt: Token by Token · an open inference lab

claims.text: Every token is a measurement.
Each study separates the system under test, workload, scenario, metric rules, validity gates and evidence boundary.

source.excerpt: each study separates the system under test, workload, scenario, metric rules, validity gates and evidence boundary

claims.text: The disclosure pattern defines the workload and system, publishes metric rules and thresholds, and states what the evidence cannot establish.

source.excerpt: define the workload and system, publish metric rules and thresholds, and state what the evidence cannot establish

claims.text: Real chat conversations without tools represent the chat slice of a mixed population.

source.expect: Real chat conversations without tools, representing the chat slice of a mixed population.

claims.text: Agentic coding request histories carry system prompts, function tools and tool output.

source.expect: Agentic coding request histories: system prompts, function tools and tool output.

claims.text: Timing distributions model tool-execution gaps and human think time.

source.expect: Timing only: tool-execution gaps and human think-time distributions for sources without timestamps.

claims.text: Issue-fix task generation and patch grading is an optional path.

source.expect: Optional issue-fix task generation and patch grading in isolated repository containers.

claims.text: A prompt pack and client-behavior profile support synthetic agent replay.

source.expect: A captured Kilo-like prompt pack and client-behavior profile for synthetic agent replay.

claims.text: Synthetic agent replay is an optional fixture.

source.expect: Optional synthetic replay fixture; provenance review required before redistribution

claims.text: An optional external generator produces tool-agent-user evaluation sessions.

source.expect: Optional external generator for tool-agent-user evaluation sessions.

claims.text: Tool-agent-user sessions are an optional integration.
A workload is resolved from a declared exact-token corpus or a versioned request corpus.

source.excerpt: Use either a declared exact-token corpus or a versioned request corpus.

claims.text: Some supported sources are not in the bundled default mix, so not every source feeds every study.

source.expect: Supported importer; not in the bundled default mix

claims.text: Requests preserve order and use recorded or modeled gaps.

source.excerpt: Requests preserve order within a slot and use recorded or modeled gaps.

claims.text: Probes are run at multiple context depths.

source.expect: Methodological reference for prompt-processing and token-generation probes at multiple context depths.

claims.text: The output policy is named before results are read.

source.excerpt: workload, output policy, sampling settings, measured loads and declared thresholds before reading results

claims.text: The client records visible time to first token, post-first-token timing, output, completion validity, failures and timestamps.

source.excerpt: The client records visible TTFT, post-first-token timing, output, completion validity, failures and timestamps.

claims.text: Engine and GPU telemetry provide context when comparable definitions are available.

source.excerpt: Engine and GPU telemetry provide request, cache, utilization, memory and power context when comparable definitions are available.

claims.text: Throughput and latency are ranked only after delivered work is comparable.
Failed or incomplete levels cannot qualify a deployment, even when surviving requests look fast.
Only tested points are reported; an unmeasured rate is not interpolated.
Unequal delivered work blocks ranking.
The public repository is on GitHub.

scenes.narration: Token by Token is an open inference lab, where every token is a measurement.

scenes.title: Why the methodology exists
scenes.narration: Numbers mean little until the system, workload, scenario, metric rules, validity gates and evidence boundary are declared.

scenes.title: The workload spectrum
scenes.narration: What enters the lab? Real chat conversations. Agentic coding with tools. Tool gaps and human think time. Optional issue-fix tasks, synthetic agent replay and tool-agent-user sessions.
on_screen: Not every source feeds every study

scenes.title: How representative load behaves
scenes.narration: Each run replays an exact-token or versioned corpus in order, with recorded or modeled gaps, declared context depth and output policy.

scenes.title: What the measurement lens sees
scenes.narration: Measurement follows the user: visible waiting, token timing, output and validity, plus engine and GPU context where definitions match.

scenes.title: Where the evidence stops
scenes.narration: Work before speed. Validity before capacity. Observed, not inferred. Unequal work blocks ranking.

scenes.title: Brand close
scenes.narration: Token by Token. Every token is a measurement.
